{{Quote|It's settled then. Tomorrow, with the Hidden Beks&ndash;the Resistance strikes back!|Haydel Goravvus, before the Resistance's doomed attempt to kill Cassus Fett|<ref name="kotor23" />}}
The '''Taris Resistance''' was the name given to the armed group of [[Taris/Legends|Tarisians]] that fought against [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] occupation during the [[Taris Siege]] in [[3963 BBY]]. After the Mandalorians stormed Taris in one of the first major offensives of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Haydel Goravvus]] retreated to Taris' [[Lower City]] and formed the Resistance out of surviving law enforcement and assorted locals, managing to hold onto a few blocks of territory despite being under constant attack by the invaders. After months of fighting, the Resistance formed a partnership with the [[Hidden Beks]], the most powerful of the [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] gangs also fighting against the Mandalorians, and with the help of Republic fugitives [[Zayne Carrick]] and [[Marn Hierogryph]], the two groups formulated a plan to deal a stunning blow to their enemies by [[Death/Legends|killing]] [[Cassus Fett]], the strategic brains behind the Mandalorian siege. But as Carrick, Hieogryph and several Resistance and Bek agents traveled to Fett's [[Jedi Tower|base]], Fett discovered the site of the [[Taris Resistance Stronghold|Resistance stronghold]] and launched a surprise attack that caught the Resistance unaware. The Resistance was quickly routed, with most of its members either being killed by the Mandalorians or fleeing into the depths of the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]] to meet violent ends at the [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] and claws of the monstrous [[rakghoul]] beasts. However, Goravvus managed to survive and flee Taris, later becoming a celebrated advocate for refugees and those at risk of war.

==Description==
{{Quote|Raana! You know the Resistance needs people&ndash;and people with the Hidden Beks' skills!|Haydel Goravvus, to Raana Tey|<ref name="kotor23" />}}
[[Taris Resistance Stronghold|Based]] out of a run-down factory in the [[Lower City]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], the Taris Resistance was the most powerful, organized and well-equipped faction fighting against the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] invaders during the [[Taris Siege]] of [[3963 BBY]]. Led by [[Haydel Goravvus]], Taris' [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]], the Taris Resistance was a motley assortment of armed locals and surviving [[Taris Civil Authority|law enforcement]] pushed into the Lower City by the Mandalorian attack.<ref name="kotor22" /> Despite Tarisian society's reputation for [[Humanocentrism]],<ref name="kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> these desperate [[Time/Legends|times]] produced a fighting force that featured many [[Alien/Legends|non-Humans]],<ref name="kotor22" /> led by Goravvus, who himself was part-[[Hamadryas]].<ref name="kotorcg">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Although the Resistance was heavily non-Human, its basis in the planet's law enforcement and the leadership role given to [[Constable/Legends|Constable]] [[Noana Sowrs]] alienated many other Tarisians fighting for their lives&mdash;although Taris was on the brink of subjugation, Sowrs still had every intention of enforcing the law against local criminals.<ref name="kotor23" />

Despite this, the Resistance found its numbers bolstered by the [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] gang known as the [[Hidden Beks]], which provided it with fighting skill and a number of swoop bikes and [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]]. The Beks made up a large part of the Resistance's force during their partnership, as the Resistance was heavily outnumbered and technologically outpaced, for instance lacking the ability to overcome Mandalorian communication jamming. Members of the Taris Resistance generally used [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], with one notable exception: the [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Raana Tey]], who fought with the Resistance using her [[Color/Legends|green]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Much of the Resistance's equipment, especially explosives, was salvaged from the Mandalorians during periodic raids on the invaders' territory. Although the Resistance was relatively well-armed, it was relatively poorly outfitted when it came to vehicles&mdash;the Resistance had access to common swoops and speeders but had almost nothing in the way of interstellar craft, save for a stealth-outfitted shuttle belonging to Raana Tey.<ref name="kotor23" />

==History==
===A new hope===
{{Quote|You know Taris. The so-called good people above&ndash;and people like us down below. Now they're down below two&ndash;and we're ''still'' beneath them. Still, I made the proffer anyway. And I was getting somewhere, too, until the constable showed up. Her family's been missing for weeks&ndash;and she blames ''all'' of us. I need something that'll get us in the door&ndash;something that'll ingratiate us with the Resistance.''"<br />"''I wish I could help you think of something.''"<br />"''Oh, you already have. ''You're'' the something.|Gadon Thek and Zayne Carrick|<ref name="kotor22" />}}
In [[3964 BBY]], the [[Mandalorian Wars]], fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]], began in earnest.<ref name="kotor8">[[Knights of the Old Republic 8|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 8]]</ref> After months of stalemated fighting along the [[Jebble-Vanquo-Tarnith line]]&mdash;a [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] security cordon meant to protect the critical [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[ecumenopolis]] of Taris, a full member of the Republic&mdash;<ref name="prime">{{KOTORbackups|0}}</ref> civil order broke down on Taris after the high-profile [[Padawan Massacre|massacre]] of the graduating class of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] at the planet's [[Jedi Tower]]. supposedly by the one surviving apprentice, [[Zayne Carrick]]. The Tower's five [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] were recalled from the planet after the deaths, an occurrence the Mandalorian [[Chief/Legends|chief]], [[Mandalore the Ultimate]], took as a signal to attack. The [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] launched a three-pronged assault aimed at taking Taris,<ref name="kotor8" /> and after the nomadic warriors had little trouble [[Battle of Vanquo|conquering]] nearby worlds such as [[Vanquo]], the stage was set for the attempt on Taris itself.<ref name="vanquo">{{CSWECite|III|294|Vanquo}}</ref> Led by master strategist [[Cassus Fett]], the Mandalorian forces first appeared in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] over Taris, and after a number of days of siege, the warriors descended onto the planet itself, facing only token resistance from swoop gangs and assorted looters in seizing the planet's [[Upper City]].<ref name="invasion">{{KOTORbackups|18}}</ref>

[[File:GoravvusStepsIn.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Haydel Goravvus intercedes in a confrontation between the Taris Resistance and the Hidden Beks.]]
With no Republic forces in sight, Tarisian Senator Haydel Goravvus disappeared from public view,<ref name="invasion" /> retreating to the Lower City to organize a resistance in the planet's depths. Establishing a base in a dilapidated Lower City factory, Goravvus managed to pull together a considerable force out of surviving law enforcement and armed Tarisian citizens, including one of Taris' top law enforcement officers, Constable Noana Sowrs, and Jedi Master Raana Tey,<ref name="kotor22" /> who had been ordered back to Taris by Republic [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]]<ref name="handbook">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Handbook]]''</ref> [[Tol Cressa]].<ref name="egtw">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Tey's arrival was crucial for the Resistance's survival, as she provided them a much-needed healer. Although the stealth-outfitted shuttle she arrived in could have provided Goravvus with a way off the planet, he elected to stay and fight, and continued to use the shuttle in operations against the Mandalorians.<ref name="kotor23" /> As the Mandalorians descended deeper into the planetwide cityscape, Goravvus' band quickly earned a reputation as the best-equipped and most well-organized faction fighting against the invaders. Other groups, separated from the main resistance by the Mandalorian invaders, continued to wage their own separate battles&mdash;chief among these was the swoop gang known as the [[Hidden Beks]], led by a man named [[Gadon Thek]].<ref name="kotor22" />

Thek, as leader of one of the most powerful and well-organized gangs on Taris, believed that Taris only had a fighting chance if he could join forces with Goravvus' resistance, but was wary of the fact that his group would still be seen as lesser criminals. With violence increasing, a dialogue commenced between the resistance and the Beks, although Constable Sowrs put the kibosh on the talks as she blamed the gangs for the disappearance of her two young children. Things changed in 3963 BBY, when Thek discovered that one of his number, [[Brejik]], had indeed kidnapped Sowrs' children against his orders&mdash;although Thek was furious, he recognized that he had been delivered the perfect bargaining chip with the Resistance. With Sowrs' son [[Nahk]] and daughter [[Tallie]] in hand, Thek and his gang fought their way through Mandalorian forces to the Resistance's base.<ref name="kotor22" /> Once Thek arrived and reunited the Sowrs family, Goravvus struck a deal with the Hidden Beks, although there was nearly violence upon their arrival, as accused Padawan killer Zayne Carrick was part of the Bek party and his death was demanded by both Tey and Resistance agent [[Shel Jelavan]], younger sister of slain Padawan [[Shad Jelavan]]. Goravvus personally stayed their hands, as neither side could afford bloodshed&mdash;Goravvus needed the numbers and skills the Beks could provide, and the Beks desperately needed medical treatment for their wounded. With that, the two factions joined forces.<ref name="kotor23" />

===The resistance strikes back===
{{Quote|You were with the Resistance?''"<br />"''As long as it lasted. We had planned to hit the Mandalorians, but it all went wrong. They ambushed ''us,'' instead. I was lucky to get my kids out. We&ndash;"<br />"''Children?'' Are they here?''"<br />"''No. There was a shuttle. I paid an Ithorian to fly them to his ship in orbit&ndash;and from there to my husband, back in the Republic. But there was only room for one more. The Senator wouldn't go, and I wouldn't leave him. So I sent a young woman along with my kids. Just in time, too. The Mandalorians kept driving us down, right into the Undercity&ndash;and the rakghouls.|[[Celeste Morne]] and Noana Sowrs after the destruction of the Resistance|<ref name="kotor25" />}}
[[File:Duelon_taris.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Resistance agents Raana Tey and Zayne Carrick duel in the Jedi Tower.]]
At the time, the Resistance was in a dire situation, with its territory reduced to only a few city blocks and its attempts to communicate to the outside constantly jammed by the Mandalorians. The arrival of the Hidden Beks was a much-needed break, as was the presence of one of Thek's acquaintances: Carrick's [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvian]] accomplice, [[Marn Hierogryph]], who carried with him a transmitter which could beat the Mandalorian jamming. Although Hierogryph's presence was only part of a plot by [[Lhosan Industries]] chairman [[Jervo Thalien]] to eliminate Goravvus&mdash;and the transmitter contained a powerful bomb&mdash;the explosive's failure to detonate allowed Goravvus to blackmail Thalien into sending aid to the front and to the Resistance. Emboldened by this development and the arrival of the Beks, Goravvus set his sights at doing major damage to the Mandalorian war effort. The Resistance learned that [[Cassus Fett]], one of Mandalore the Ultimate's chief [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]], had set up shop at the former Jedi Tower to personally oversee planetary operations. With that in mind, Goravvus, Sowrs and Thek planned to eliminate Fett and throw the Mandalorian siege effort into chaos&mdash;while they lacked the numbers to directly assault the Tower, they had salvaged demolition charges in a recent raid on Mandalorian territory, and Hierogryph's transmitter-cum-bomb contained a detonator that Hierogryph's acquaintance [[Del Moomo]] was able to get working again. Although it seemed like a simple task to simply destroy the Jedi Tower with the newfound munitions, Carrick argued that a same-day reconnaissance mission on the Tower was needed, in order to ensure that Fett was still at the Tower and wasn't holding captives. As the three people present with the most experience in the Jedi Tower, Carrick, Jelavan and Master Tey were dispatched to the Tower, although Tey and Jelavan secretly plotted to eliminate Carrick once there.<ref name="kotor23" />

Disguised as a Mandalorian warrior and a captured saboteur, Carrick and Jelavan gained entrance to the Jedi Tower as Thek, Moomo, Brejik and Hierogryph set up the charges down below. Jelavan, who was having doubts about Carrick's guilt, hesitated when the time came to strike him down and allowed him to go on ahead, and Carrick reached the top only to find that Fett had pulled out an [[Standard hour|hour before]]&mdash;he had determined where in the Lower City the Resistance had holed up, and had gone to carry out a decisive strike. The Mandalorian ambush was devastating, scattering the Resistance survivors, many of whom attempted to fall back to the Hidden Bek hideout known as [[The Pit (Taris)|the Pit]]. While Brejik and Del Moomo veered off to join the fight in the Lower City, Thek and Hierogryph made a daring run through Mandalorian fire to the top of the Jedi Tower in an attempt to save Carrick and Jelavan. The two Resistance agents managed to grab hold of Thek's speeder's tow cable&mdash;but after Hierogryph saw a wounded Tey ignite her lightsaber in an apparent attempt to attack Carrick, he detonated the charges anyway and destroyed the Jedi Tower.<ref name="kotor24">[[Knights of the Old Republic 24|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 24]]</ref>

The four survivors returned to the Lower City to find the Resistance in chaos. Although Tey's stealth-equipped shuttle might have provided an escape for Senator Goravvus, he refused to abandon Taris&mdash;instead, Shel Jelavan took the ship off the planet with Constable Sowrs' children. Meanwhile, the Mandalorians relentlessly pushed on, driving the Resistance down even further, into the [[rakghoul]]-infested wasteland known as the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]]. The [[Rakghoul plague/Legends|diseased beasts]] spelled death for many of the scattered Resistance survivors, including Constable Sowrs. Although the Resistance was effectively crushed, some managed to outlast the Mandalorian assault: Carrick and Hierogryph escaped certain death at the hands of the rakghouls and make it off the planet with the help of [[Jedi Shadow]] [[Celeste Morne]], while Gadon Thek and Brejik survived to keep the Hidden Beks going through the siege and in the years after.<ref name="kotor25" />

==Members==
{{Quote|You have good people who work for you, Gadon. Would you leave ''them'' in their hour of need?|Haydel Goravvus|<ref name="kotor23" />}}
[[File:Goravvus-KOTOR1.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Haydel Goravvus, founder and leader of the Taris Resistance.]]
The Taris Resistance was headed by Haydel Goravvus, the half-[[Human/Legends|Human]], half-Hamadryas [[Politics/Legends|politician]] who represented Taris in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] at the time of the Mandalorian invasion.<ref name="kotorcg" /> Although Goravvus attained his seat through a corrupt partnership with Jervo Thalien and Lhosan Industries, he realized once in office that he was more interested in the people than the profits and, against all odds, grew into a selfless public servant.<ref name="kotor23" /> When the Mandalorians attacked and social order broke down on Taris, Goravvus retreated out of the public eye<ref name="invasion" /> and into the Lower City, where he formed the Taris Resistance out of survivors and law enforcement willing to fight for their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Although Goravvus had several chances to escape the planet during the Mandalorian siege, the Senator refused to leave his people behind,<ref name="kotor23" /> even after Cassus Fett's surprise attack effectively crushed his rebel group.<ref name="kotor25" /> Goravvus was eventually forced to leave Taris as the Mandalorians further consolidated control of the planet, and survived in [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] to become a popular activist for refugees and people living on occupied worlds.<ref name="kotorcg" />

Goravvus' resistance drew much of its military force from the remnants of Taris' law enforcement, which was helmed by [[Sector Constable]] Noana Sowrs.<ref name="kotor23" /> Although Sowrs complicated Goravvus' attempt to parley with local swoop gangs with her intractable desire to continue enforcing the law during the Mandalorian siege,<ref name="kotor22" /> she loyally served Goravvus as one of his top [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]] throughout the Taris Siege. The fate of Sowrs' two children, Nahk and Tallie, became crucial to the Taris Resistance's eventual partnership with the Hidden Beks gang, despite Sowrs' hostility to whom she saw as underworld criminals.<ref name="kotor23" /> Sowrs' children had been in fact kidnapped by Hidden Beks member Brejik against the order of gang leader Gadon Thek&mdash;once Thek discovered that his protege had done this, he grudgingly realized that he had been handed the perfect bargaining chip with the Resistance,<ref name="kotor22" /> and returning the Sowrs children helped ensure a partnership would be struck.<ref name="kotor23" /> Sowrs' reunion with her children was, however, brief. Cassus Fett's ambush forced Sowrs to send her children offworld, and the Constable was killed soon after by Undercity rakghouls.<ref name="kotor25" />

Joining Constable Sowrs at Goravvus' side was the unstable Togruta Jedi Master named Raana Tey,<ref name="kotor23" /> who had in fact been one of the five Jedi Masters originally stationed at the Taris Jedi Tower before the Padawan Massacre. Unbeknownst to the greater galaxy, Tey and the Jedi Tower Masters were part of a secret [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] cabal known as the [[Jedi Covenant]] that was dedicated to foreseeing the return of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].<ref name="kotor9">[[Knights of the Old Republic 9|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 9]]</ref> Shortly before the Mandalorian attack,<ref name="kotor22" /> a misinterpreted [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] led Tey and her compatriots to murder their Jedi Padawans and pin the massacre on the lone survivor, Zayne Carrick.<ref name="kotor5">[[Knights of the Old Republic 5|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 5]]</ref> The Jedi were pulled offworld after the attack, but Tey was ordered back to Taris alone by Supreme Chancellor<ref name="kotor23" /> Tol Cressa<ref name="egtw" /> after the siege began. Tey linked up with Goravvus' Resistance and served a vital role as a healer,<ref name="kotor23" /> but lacking the support system she needed due to her uncontrolled Force visions, she descended into insanity during the battle.<ref name="handbook" /> Tey befriended Resistance agent Shel Jelavan&mdash;whose brother Shad was one of the murdered Padawans&mdash;and Tey plotted to use Jelavan to murder Carrick once she re-encountered the fugitive former Padawan on Taris.<ref name="kotor23" /> However, Jelavan turned on Tey when she realized the truth, and Tey was killed in the explosion of the Jedi Tower.<ref name="kotor24" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Taris Resistance first appeared in [[Knights of the Old Republic 22|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 22]], an issue of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'']], written by [[John Jackson Miller]] and released in [[2007]].<ref name="kotor22" /> The Resistance, which originally mentioned in the series' [[Knights of the Old Republic 21|previous issue]],<ref name="kotor21">[[Knights of the Old Republic 21|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 21]]</ref> played a central part in the [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Knights of Suffering|''Knights of Suffering'']] story arc<ref name="kotor23" /><ref name="kotor24" /> and would later be mentioned in several more issues of ''Knights of the Old Republic''.<ref name="kotor25" />
